benchmark_details.name: General Meeting Minutes
benchmark_details.overview: Extract names, locations, signatures from table-like meeting minutes of Mines de Costano S.A., 1951-1968

purpose_and_intended_users.goal: Measure how well vision-language models turn the attendance registers of a company's general meetings, printed forms filled in by typewriter and by hand, into structured records: one row per shareholder with name and address split apart, share counts by class, votes, and the presence and text of a signature, plus the carried-forward totals. The results are meant to guide historians, archivists and digital humanities projects in choosing a model for digitising tabular business records.
tasks: splitting a combined name-and-address cell into two fields
detection and transcription of handwritten signatures
transcription of share counts and page totals
purpose_and_intended_users.limitations:
Nine pages from the registers of a single company, 1951–1968, 85 rows in all; results do not transfer automatically to other forms, hands or record types. Several images are two-page spreads, so the number of rows per image varies from 6 to 20.

The scorer has several blind spots:

- Rows are compared by position (`entries[0]` with `entries[0]`), not by row number or name. A model that skips or inserts one row is scored against the wrong ground-truth row for every row after it.
- Only fields present in the ground truth are scored. Rows the model adds beyond the last ground-truth row cost nothing.
- About a fifth of the scored fields are empty strings (empty share columns, missing totals, absent signatures); a model that returns `""` there scores 1.0 for them.
- `document` and `page_number` are given in the prompt, so they are close to free points.
- A wrong `signature_present` value scores 0.22, not 0, because the booleans are compared as the strings `True` and `False`.
- Scores are similarities, not matches: a field that is 80% similar contributes 0.8, so mean scores look higher than a thresholded F1 would.

Some ground truths write the degree sign as the literal text `U+00B0` (15 times on four pages), so a model that writes `°` loses a little similarity in those addresses.
out_of_scope_uses: evaluating signature verification or writer identification
evaluating arithmetic on the share columns (totals must be transcribed, not computed)
drawing conclusions about the shareholders named in the registers

data.source: Attendance registers of the general meetings of Mines de Costano S.A., the company that operated the gold mine of Sessa (Malcantone, Ticino) from 1933, from the company's private archive. Each page is a printed form with the columns *N° d'ordre*, *Nom, prénoms et domicile des actionnaires*, *Actions* (two columns, *de priorité* and *ordinaire*, whose order varies between forms), *Nombre de voix* and *Signature des actionnaires ou des mandataires*, with a carried-forward total (*report*, *à reporter*). Names and addresses are typed; share counts and totals are typed or handwritten; signatures are handwritten.
data.format:
One JPG per page or two-page spread, about 2480×3200 px and 0.9–2 MB. The ground truth is one JSON file per image, following the `MinutesPage` dataclass in `dataclass.py`:

```json
{
  "document": "Se_19_Assemblée Mine d. Costano_2.9_12.1962_page_4",
  "page_number": 4,
  "entries": [
    {
      "number": "1",
      "name": "M. BREHAM Alain",
      "address": "45 Boulevard Charcot - Neuilly s/Seine (Seine",
      "actions_o": "179",
      "actions_p": "520",
      "no_de_voix": "699",
      "signature_present": true,
      "signature": "Pa"
    }
  ],
  "total_actions": {"total_o": "659", "total_p": "2310", "total_voix": "2964"}
}
```

- `document`, `page_number`: taken from the file name and passed to the model in the prompt
- `entries`: one object per table row; `name` and `address` come from the same cell and are split into two fields; every value except `signature_present` is a string, empty when the cell is empty
- `total_actions`: the totals written at the foot of the page, empty strings where none are written
data.annotation: Ground truths were transcribed and curated by hand by the annotator Sven Lienhard (see Contributors by Role): diplomatic transcription without added accents, line breaks inside addresses kept, the dash separating name and address removed, totals transcribed only where written on the page.
data.collection_date: Not specified for benchmark collection or digitisation. Source-document dates: The file names date the registers from 1951 to 1968 (1951, 1961, 1962, 1965, 1967, 1968); for the `Bilanz` files the year may be that of the balance sheet rather than of the meeting.
data.contamination_controls: No held-out private split, training-data audit or other contamination control is documented. Inputs, prompts and ground truths are distributed together in this public repository. Whether any evaluated model saw these materials during training is unknown.

methods: zero-shot structured extraction from a single page image per request, with the file name and page number given in the prompt
structured JSON output requested using the `MinutesPage` dataclass
benchmark default output cap of 40,960 tokens; test rules can override it and model-specific ceilings can lower it

five prompt variants: `prompt.txt` (short instructions on splitting name and address) is the main cross-model variant; `extended_prompt.txt`, `prompt_first_reformulated.txt`, `updated_prompt.txt` and `updated_prompt_steps.txt` (longer rules on transcription fidelity, column order, totals and signatures) each have three configured tests. No controlled prompt comparison with identified runs is reported here. Scores are comparable across models only within one prompt
no shared context: nothing in `context/` is sent, and signatures are scored as ordinary fields
methodology.calculation:
For each page, every terminal field of the ground-truth JSON is enumerated (`document`, `page_number`, `entries[i].*`, `total_actions.*`) and the response value at the same path is compared with it:

- identical values (including two empty strings, or the same number as integer and string) score 1.0
- a value missing from the response (path absent or `null`) scores 0.0
- otherwise the score is the rapidfuzz `ratio` of the two values as strings, divided by 100, case-sensitive and unnormalised

The page score is the unrounded mean over its fields; the benchmark score is the mean of the page scores, so every page weighs the same whatever its number of rows. A response that is not parseable JSON is left out of the mean rather than scored as zero.
methodology.interpretation: Scores range from 0 to 1; higher is better. Partial similarity earns partial credit and empty fields are easy to match, so absolute scores run high; compare models with each other rather than against a fixed bar. A low score on one page often means a skipped or inserted row rather than poor reading, because the rows after it are misaligned.
methodology.baseline_results: Model results are available on the [benchmark page](https://rise-services.rise.unibas.ch/benchmarks/p/benchmarks/general_meeting_minutes) and in `results/<date>/<test_id>/` at the repository root. Compare runs with the same prompt, scoring rules and ground-truth revision, and report the number of successfully scored objects alongside the score. No fixed model baseline with a run ID and date is specified here.
methodology.validation: The ground truths were created by the annotator and domain experts listed under Contributors by Role; no separate second check is recorded. Scoring is deterministic.

ethical_and_legal_considerations.privacy_and_anonymity: The registers name shareholders and their proxies, private persons and companies, with their home addresses, share holdings and signatures, 1951–1968. They are not anonymised. These are company records of shareholdings, and no personal-rights issue is seen in publishing them.
ethical_and_legal_considerations.compliance_with_regulations: The registers come from the company's private archive, so no public archival law sets a protection period for them; they are used under the archive's grant of free use. No separate reuse terms are stated for the ground truths. No ethical review was carried out.
